q: The compact-open topology on the function space C(X,Y) (continuous maps from X to Y) is generated by the sub-basic sets K(K,U) = {f : f(K) ⊆ U} for K compact in X and U open in Y. When X is locally compact Hausdorff, the evaluation map:
opts: ev: C(X,Y) × X → Y is continuous with the compact-open topology
ev is only continuous when Y = ℝ
exp: The compact-open topology makes evaluation continuous (when X is locally compact Hausdorff). This makes it the natural topology for function spaces; for example, C(X,ℝ) with compact-open topology is a locally convex topological vector space.
